## What's in the prompt

The system prompt defines **SolarGuide**, your support chatbot, structured using standard system-prompt design patterns:

| Section | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Role & Identity** | Sets persona, company, and tone anchors |
| **Mission** | Gives a north star for every interaction |
| **Capabilities** | Explicit list of answerable topics (products, quotes, installs, warranties, troubleshooting, monitoring, billing, service) |
| **Behavior Guidelines** | Empathetic, honest, plain-language rules — including "never fabricate" and privacy protections |
| **Response Format** | Enforces the greeting → steps → next-action structure with a worked example |
| **Escalation Rules** | Clear triggers for human handoff (safety, legal, disputes, stuck troubleshooting) |
| **Boundaries & Compliance** | Keeps the bot out of financial/tax/utility-advice liability |
| **Edge Cases & Fallbacks** | Angry customers, unknown answers, off-topic queries, accessibility |
| **Verification Checklist** | A self-check the model can run before each reply |

## Suggested next steps

1. **Add real product data** — swap the placeholder specs (panel models, warranty terms) for your actual SKUs and policies so answers are grounded.
2. **Wire it to your knowledge base** — paste in your help-center articles or RAG context so the bot can cite real documentation.
3. **Few-shot examples** — add 2–3 logged real conversations (troubleshooting + billing + escalation) to the end of the prompt to anchor the tone.
4. **A/B test** — run two variants (e.g., with vs. without the checklist) against a set of ~30 representative tickets and measure resolution rate and escalation rate.
5. **Version it** — commit the prompt file to your repo and tag versions so changes are trackable.
